name: Victor Anders
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember sitting first in an empty waiting room.” People around the approach to Seabright Court know Victor by a small Tuesday habit. Victor likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I arrived at the dentist six hours early and left with a vacancy on his cleaning crew.
appearance: Back on the street, look for a narrow-striped sweater and a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. Victor has one cheek that creases before the other, with black hair twisted into a small knot. Victor squares up pieces of paper while thinking during a conversation.
personality: Victor prefers exact instructions at work and pleasant surprises at home. The two standards occasionally collide, especially when a relative thinks dropping by counts as notice.
agenda: To get the times for the new cleaning shift right.
family: Elsa Guzman is Victor’s older cousin. Victor offers the first invitation. Elsa gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The waiting-room plant*, Elsa says, “I never have visitors. I booked the plant for Thursday and three gardeners turned up.”
connections: Lorenzo Mack (clock setter). The tide setter shows the worker exactly what time the wall never promised.

reactions.situation: A supervisor blames the new hire for missing the time
reactions.response: Victor checks which dial the worker saw before accepting a lateness entry.

reactions.situation: An envelope of wages is found under a café chair
reactions.response: Victor finds a second person to witness its return so an honest mistake won't cost a worker their pay.
